solution:
Use the defactorization formula \(2\sin A\cos B = \sin(A + B) + \sin(A - B)\), with \(A = 4x\), \(B = 2x\).
\(2\sin 4x\cos 2x = \sin(4x + 2x) + \sin(4x - 2x)\)
\(= \sin 6x + \sin 2x\)

Use the defactorization formula \(2\sin A\cos B = \sin(A + B) + \sin(A - B)\), with \(A = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\), \(B = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\).
Here \(A + B = \dfrac{2\pi}{3} + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{7\pi}{6}\) and \(A - B = \dfrac{2\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\).
\(2\sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} = \sin\dfrac{7\pi}{6} + \sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}\)
Check: \(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} = 0\) makes the left side \(0\), and \(\sin\dfrac{7\pi}{6} + \sin\dfrac{\pi}{6} = -\dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} = 0\).
\(\therefore\ 2\sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\cos\dfrac{\pi}{2} = \sin\dfrac{7\pi}{6} + \sin\dfrac{\pi}{6}\)

Use the defactorization formula \(2\cos A\cos B = \cos(A + B) + \cos(A - B)\), with \(A = 4\theta\), \(B = 2\theta\).
\(2\cos 4\theta\cos 2\theta = \cos(4\theta + 2\theta) + \cos(4\theta - 2\theta)\)
\(= \cos 6\theta + \cos 2\theta\)

Use the defactorization formula \(2\cos A\cos B = \cos(A + B) + \cos(A - B)\), with \(A = 35^\circ\), \(B = 75^\circ\).
\(2\cos 35^\circ\cos 75^\circ = \cos(35^\circ + 75^\circ) + \cos(35^\circ - 75^\circ)\)
\(= \cos 110^\circ + \cos(-40^\circ)\)
Since \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\),
\(= \cos 110^\circ + \cos 40^\circ\)

L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{\sin 2x + \sin 2y}{\sin 2x - \sin 2y}\)
Apply the factorization formulae \(\sin C + \sin D = 2\sin\dfrac{C+D}{2}\cos\dfrac{C-D}{2}\) and \(\sin C - \sin D = 2\cos\dfrac{C+D}{2}\sin\dfrac{C-D}{2}\), with \(C = 2x\), \(D = 2y\):
\(= \dfrac{2\sin(x + y)\cos(x - y)}{2\cos(x + y)\sin(x - y)}\)
\(= \dfrac{\sin(x + y)}{\cos(x + y)}\times\dfrac{\cos(x - y)}{\sin(x - y)}\)
\(= \tan(x + y)\cot(x - y)\)
\(= \dfrac{\tan(x + y)}{\tan(x - y)} = \) R.H.S.

Group the two terms whose arguments differ by \(4x\).
L.H.S. \(= (\sin 6x - \sin 2x) + \sin 4x\)
Using \(\sin C - \sin D = 2\cos\dfrac{C+D}{2}\sin\dfrac{C-D}{2}\) and \(\sin 4x = 2\sin 2x\cos 2x\),
\(= 2\cos 4x\sin 2x + 2\sin 2x\cos 2x\)
\(= 2\sin 2x\,(\cos 4x + \cos 2x)\)
Using \(\cos C + \cos D = 2\cos\dfrac{C+D}{2}\cos\dfrac{C-D}{2}\),
\(= 2\sin 2x\,(2\cos 3x\cos x)\)
\(= 4\cos x\,\sin 2x\,\cos 3x = \) R.H.S.

Numerator \(= (\sin x + \sin 5x) - (\sin 3x + \sin 7x)\)
\(= 2\sin 3x\cos 2x - 2\sin 5x\cos 2x\)
\(= 2\cos 2x\,(\sin 3x - \sin 5x) = 2\cos 2x\,(-2\cos 4x\sin x) = -4\sin x\cos 2x\cos 4x\)
Denominator \(= (\cos x - \cos 3x) - (\cos 5x - \cos 7x)\)
\(= 2\sin 2x\sin x - 2\sin 6x\sin x\)
\(= 2\sin x\,(\sin 2x - \sin 6x) = 2\sin x\,(-2\cos 4x\sin 2x) = -4\sin x\sin 2x\cos 4x\)
\(\therefore\) L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{-4\sin x\cos 2x\cos 4x}{-4\sin x\sin 2x\cos 4x} = \dfrac{\cos 2x}{\sin 2x}\)
\(= \cot 2x = \) R.H.S.

Multiply each side by \(2\) and use \(2\sin A\cos B = \sin(A + B) + \sin(A - B)\).
\(2\times\) L.H.S. \(= 2\sin 18^\circ\cos 39^\circ + 2\sin 6^\circ\cos 15^\circ\)
\(= [\sin 57^\circ + \sin(-21^\circ)] + [\sin 21^\circ + \sin(-9^\circ)]\)
\(= \sin 57^\circ - \sin 21^\circ + \sin 21^\circ - \sin 9^\circ = \sin 57^\circ - \sin 9^\circ\)
\(2\times\) R.H.S. \(= 2\sin 24^\circ\cos 33^\circ = \sin 57^\circ + \sin(-9^\circ) = \sin 57^\circ - \sin 9^\circ\)
Both sides reduce to the same expression, so dividing by \(2\),
\(\sin 18^\circ\cos 39^\circ + \sin 6^\circ\cos 15^\circ = \sin 24^\circ\cos 33^\circ = \) R.H.S.

Since \(\cos 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}\),
L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{1}{2}\cos 20^\circ\,(\cos 40^\circ\cos 80^\circ)\)
By \(2\cos A\cos B = \cos(A + B) + \cos(A - B)\):
\(2\cos 40^\circ\cos 80^\circ = \cos 120^\circ + \cos 40^\circ = \cos 40^\circ - \dfrac{1}{2}\)
\(2\cos 20^\circ\cos 40^\circ = \cos 60^\circ + \cos 20^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2} + \cos 20^\circ\)
Hence
L.H.S. \(= \dfrac{1}{2}\cos 20^\circ\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\cos 40^\circ - \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\cos 20^\circ\cos 40^\circ - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos 20^\circ\right)\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{4}\left[\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2} + \cos 20^\circ\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos 20^\circ\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{2}\cos 20^\circ - \dfrac{1}{2}\cos 20^\circ\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}\times\dfrac{1}{4}\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{16} = \) R.H.S.

L.H.S. \(= \sin 60^\circ\,\sin 20^\circ\,(\sin 40^\circ\sin 80^\circ)\)
By \(2\sin A\sin B = \cos(A - B) - \cos(A + B)\):
\(2\sin 40^\circ\sin 80^\circ = \cos 40^\circ - \cos 120^\circ = \cos 40^\circ + \dfrac{1}{2}\)
By \(2\sin A\cos B = \sin(A + B) + \sin(A - B)\):
\(2\sin 20^\circ\cos 40^\circ = \sin 60^\circ + \sin(-20^\circ) = \sin 60^\circ - \sin 20^\circ\)
Hence
L.H.S. \(= \sin 60^\circ\sin 20^\circ\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}\left(\cos 40^\circ + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\sin 60^\circ\left(\sin 20^\circ\cos 40^\circ + \dfrac{1}{2}\sin 20^\circ\right)\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\sin 60^\circ\left[\dfrac{1}{2}(\sin 60^\circ - \sin 20^\circ) + \dfrac{1}{2}\sin 20^\circ\right]\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{2}\sin 60^\circ\times\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{4}\sin^{2}60^\circ\)
\(= \dfrac{1}{4}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^{2} = \dfrac{1}{4}\times\dfrac{3}{4}\)
\(= \dfrac{3}{16} = \) R.H.S.
